- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slowly rising, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates upside; add 2–5% to forecast mean to reflect supply constraint + sentiment lag.  
- When sentiment turns bearish (≤0.00) and model continues rising, reverse trend by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows mean reversion after 10–15 days, model often fails to reflect it; apply 0.5–1.5% downward correction after day 10.  
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (≥3/30d), model tends to underreact; add 1–3% to forecast to account for supply shock lag.  
- When bullish sentiment is high but model forecast is flat, assume sentiment is “overvalued” — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.
